packet.prompt:
Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

text:
PACKET-11 - UNVERIFIED IMAGE READING (blind; no identification was revealed to me by prior context)

LAYOUT SURVEY (image only)
The packet shows several very small torn scraps, each photographed on a dark
ground above a Munsell linear gray scale with mm rule (label "230417").
image-001, -003, -005 are reduced overviews (scrap + scale); image-002, -004,
-006 are close crops of the scrap in the preceding overview. Further images
described below as viewed.

Scrap A (image-001 overview, image-002 crop): c. 5 x 9 mm on the mm rule, fibrous
torn edges, paper-like fibres. One short red vertical stroke at upper right
(observation; possibly a paragraph mark or rubric stroke - tentative). Brown ink
traces on about four levels; no complete letter is certain.
Scrap B (image-003 overview, image-004 crop): c. 38 x 17 mm. Two ruled vertical
lines in brown ink run through it, enclosing a blank band (observation; tentative
interpretation: an intercolumnar space, so the scrap preserves the right edge of
one column and the left edge of the next). Red ink: a dot/stroke at the top of
the right part and a large red paraph-like or initial-like curved sign at the
bottom of the right part.
Scrap C (image-005 overview, image-006 crop): narrow vertical strip c. 8 x 27 mm,
five line-levels of brown ink, a gothic book hand; no ruling or red visible.

No running title, heading, or gloss is visible on any scrap; the crops are far
too small to show page layout beyond the two vertical rules on scrap B.

TRANSCRIPTION

Scrap A - image-002 (crop)
image-002 line 1: [illegible - ink traces] followed by a red vertical stroke
image-002 line 2: [illegible; perhaps two or three minims with a cross-stroke]
image-002 line 3: [illegible traces]
image-002 line 4: [illegible traces; possibly "e" or "c"?]
(Nothing connected can be read from this scrap.)

Scrap B - image-004 (crop); image-003 shows the same scrap reduced
Left part (end of lines of a left-hand column, left of the first ruled line):
image-004 line 1: ]auit(?) or ]uilla(?)  [minims + tall final stroke with an abbreviation hook above; reading very uncertain, could be "]aulla'" / "]mil(ite)r"?]
image-004 line 2: ]= ad      [a line-filler or hyphen-like double stroke at the torn left edge, then "ad" with a curved abbreviation/ascender stroke above the a]
image-004 line 3: ]nc        [only the lower left; "]nc" or "]ne"; a long thin diagonal pen stroke runs to its right across the blank band]
Blank band between the two ruled verticals: no text.
Right part (beginnings of lines of a right-hand column):
image-004 line 1: [red dot/stroke and a black trace at the torn top edge: "o"? or "e"?] [illegible]
image-004 line 2: vatas(?) / v(er)itas(?)   [letters read as: r-shaped or v first letter, "a"/"e", "t", "a", "s" - i.e. "ratas"? "vatas"? "v'tas"?; final letter is a round s or "o"]
image-004 line 3: tione[   ("tione", clear; torn after e)
image-004 line 4: [large red sign, like a paraph or an "A"/alpha-shaped initial] then a black horizontal stroke and "i"/"l" with strokes: "-1-"? [illegible, cut by the tear]

Scrap C - image-006 (crop); image-005 shows the same scrap reduced
image-006 line 1: ]oni[ or ]om[   (round letter + minims; "oin"/"om"/"oni"?)
image-006 line 2: ]L(?) i[ or ]t . l[   (a letter like a capital L or a long-footed "c/t", then an upright stroke)
image-006 line 3: ]c(?) &(?) [   (trace at left edge; then a sign resembling "&"/"et" or a "g"/"z"-like form)
image-006 line 4: ]reu[ or ]teri[   (r/t + e + two minims with a descending stroke)
image-006 line 5: ]x[ or ]p(er)?[   (crossed strokes like "x")

Scrap D - image-008 (crop); image-007 shows the same scrap reduced
Narrow strip c. 8 x 27 mm, heavily abraded/fibrous; only one line-level keeps ink.
image-008 line 1: [faint traces only, upper third]
image-008 line 2: ]x(?) l .[   (a small crossed form like "x" or a tironian-style sign, then a tall upright "l"/"i" with a foot, then a dot or the start of a round letter)
Remaining two thirds of the strip: no ink visible (surface lost or blank).

Scrap E - image-010 (crop); image-009 shows the same scrap reduced
Layout: scrap c. 12 x 30 mm mounted on a square of thin translucent tissue
(c. 48 x 46 mm; the tissue to the right is blank). Six line-levels of a small
cursive/bookhand in brown ink, preserved as line-beginnings (left edge torn,
right edge torn straight). Red: a small red paraph-like mark at the left of
line 3 and a red stroke filling the capital Q of line 3 (observation; tentative
interpretation: a new sentence or section opens at "Qu..."). A cross-shaped
sign with a horizontal bar stands between lines 1 and 2 below "sup" (it may be
the descender-crossing of "p" = "sup(er)" continued downward, or an insertion/
reference sign - uncertain).
image-010 line 0: [tops cut away; traces of two letters at the torn upper edge]
image-010 line 1: sup(er)? eu(m)?[      ("sup" with crossed descender, then "eu" with a horizontal abbreviation stroke above = "eu(m)" or "en("; torn after)
image-010 line 2: no(n) pr[             ("no" with macron; then "p" with crossed descender + superscript/abbreviated letter: "p(ro)"/"p(er)"/"pri"? torn)
image-010 line 3: [red paraph] Qui[     (capital Q touched with red; "Qui" or "Qua"/"Quo"; torn after the third letter)
image-010 line 4: ]xit(?) di[ / ]uit ili[  (first group "vit"/"xit"/"nit" with its first letter cut by the left tear; second group begins with a tall stroke: "di"/"ih"/"ill")
image-010 line 5: ]o(?) di[             (a round letter, a 2-shaped/"z"-like sign above or before it possibly an abbreviation or "et", then "di")
image-010 line 6: dic(?)[ / dix(?)[     ("di" followed by a stroke rising to the right; torn)

SELECTION AND WHAT REMAINS UNREAD
All ten images were viewed (five overviews, five crops). Every scrap was
attempted in full; nothing was deliberately skipped. No span of connected text
exists: the largest scraps (B and E) give at most one to two words per line
over four to six lines. The securely legible strings are "tione" (B, right
part, line 3), "ad" (B, left part, line 2), "no(n)" and a red-touched "Qu.."
(E, lines 2-3), and "sup.. eu.." (E, line 1).

LIMITATIONS
- Scraps A, C, D carry only isolated letters; readings there are guesses at letter shapes.
- Only one face of each scrap is shown; I cannot say whether the versos carry text.
- Whether the five scraps come from one leaf, and their relative order, cannot be determined from the images. Scrap B's hand (rounder, larger) and scrap E's hand (smaller, more cursive) look different to me (tentative).
- Scrap orientation is as photographed; scraps A, C, D could be rotated.
- A wider view is not possible (these are the whole scraps); raking-light or verso images of scraps B and E would be the useful additions.
- I did nothing beyond the rules: opened only PROMPT.md and the ten image files of this packet.
